A_root_cause_of_the_404.actual_cause: customer_site pages are published as a STATIC GitHub Pages tree. The beacon posted to a same-origin relative '/api/page-view', which on that host resolves to https://galaxyaek7-del.github.io/api/page-view and returns HTTP 404 because Pages serves files and has no Express handler. The Express receiver only runs in the Node process, which has no public URL (verified: .env contains no public base URL).
A_root_cause_of_the_404.why_it_was_invisible: every one of the 58 inline beacons ended in .catch(()=>{}) / .catch(function(){}) - a silent swallow. A 404 and a success were indistinguishable, so 'no visitors' and 'no measurement' looked identical.

my_own_defects_this_cycle_disclosed: First implementation substituted the tag in place, which nested <script src> INSIDE an open <script> block on pages whose beacon sat inside a larger script (about.html). That is invalid and would never execute. My original balance check passed it because one <script> and one </script> were added. Caught by inspecting the rendered result, reverted with git checkout, and reimplemented with an explicit _inside_script() guard.

The first _inside_script() guard then produced 58 false positives because rfind('<script') matched the inserted tag's OWN opening tag, making the check compare the tag against itself. Fixed by passing the start of the whole tag rather than the offset of the path inside it.

A verification check of '"/api/page-view" in text AND "fetch(" in text' flagged affiliate-standing-desks.html falsely, because that page's explanatory comment still names the route. Replaced with a precise re-scan for surviving beacon statements.
